items.title: Eurozone inflation rises to 4%, its highest in three years
items.why: Prices in the countries using the euro rose 4.0% in the year to October, up from 3.8% in September, Eurostat's first estimate shows. Energy prices were up 20.8%. Lithuania had the highest rate, 6.1%, and Malta the lowest, 2.3%.
items.matters: Markets now expect the European Central Bank to raise interest rates again in December, making borrowing dearer.

items.title: Shares rise in Europe and US after Democrats win Congress
items.why: European shares and US stock futures rose on Wednesday after Democrats won both houses of Congress, AP and CNBC report, as investors expect gridlock and fewer sudden policy changes. Japan's Nikkei closed 1.4% lower on AI-chip worries. Gold rose almost 3% and the dollar weakened.
items.matters: Clean-energy shares rose and defence shares fell, as investors weighed how a Democratic Congress could change US spending.
items.changed: Updated: European shares and US futures rose after the early fall in Asia.

items.title: South Africans vote in local elections seen as test for ANC
items.why: Polls opened at 07:00 local time on Wednesday across South Africa for municipal elections, with a record 29.2 million people registered, the electoral commission says. Voters choose councils for 257 municipalities, including eight big metros. Final results are expected on Sunday.
items.matters: The ANC lost its national majority in 2024, and polls suggest its support could fall below 40%, leaving more cities to coalitions.

items.title: Iran says four oil tankers destroyed by mines near Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say four oil tankers hit naval mines on Wednesday while using a route Iran has banned, south of the Strait of Hormuz, and were still burning; two other ships were halted. The claim has not been independently confirmed.
items.matters: Iran's supreme leader warned of a much wider war if attacks resume; Trump says he has no immediate plans for new strikes.

items.title: Democrats win control of US House and Senate
items.why: Democrats will control both the House of Representatives and the Senate after Tuesday's midterm elections, AP projects, winning at least 54 Senate seats. They took at least seven Republican-held Senate seats, including Texas, Maine and Kansas. Races in Alaska and Mississippi are still being counted.
items.matters: Trump says he is 'absolutely willing' to accept the results; from January, Democrats can block his bills and open investigations.
items.changed: Updated: Democrats reach at least 54 Senate seats; Trump says he accepts the results.

items.title: PSG beat Villarreal 6-0 as Barcelona and Bayern win in Champions League
items.why: Paris Saint-Germain won 6-0 away at Villarreal on 3 November, scoring four goals in the first 17 minutes, a competition record according to Opta. Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, Bayern Munich won 2-0 at Atletico Madrid, and Manchester United came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2.
items.matters: PSG lead the league phase with 12 points after four matches; the remaining matchday 4 games are played on Wednesday.

items.title: AMD's sales jump 45% as demand for AI chips nearly doubles
items.why: The US chipmaker AMD said third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.4 billion, with its data-centre business, which sells AI processors, up 97% to a record $8.5 billion. It expects about $17 billion in sales this quarter, and its shares rose about 8% after hours.
items.matters: It suggests companies are still spending heavily on AI computing, even as investors worry about whether that spending will pay off.

items.title: Spain's transport minister resigns after train crash that killed 69
items.why: Óscar Puente resigned on Tuesday, six days after a high-speed train hit a stationary train near Urda, south of Madrid, on 28 October. Spanish authorities give a provisional toll of 69 dead. Puente said a minister could not stay after two such serious crashes in a year.
items.matters: Investigators are examining why controllers let the train continue after a safety system failed, Euronews and Al Jazeera report.

items.title: Catalan writer Cristina Fernández Cubas wins the Cervantes Prize
items.why: Spain's culture minister, Ernest Urtasun, announced on 3 November that Cristina Fernández Cubas, born in 1945 in Arenys de Mar near Barcelona, has won the 2026 Cervantes Prize. The jury praised her short stories and fantastic fiction. The prize is worth €125,000.
items.matters: It is the top award for literature in Spanish, and she is only the seventh woman to win it since 1976.

items.title: False bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe
items.why: At least seven flights to Poland, Italy, Spain and Bulgaria were searched or diverted on Tuesday after bomb threats, and a cruise ship bound for Israel was evacuated off the Greek island of Syros. No explosives were found and all the planes landed safely.
items.matters: No one has claimed responsibility, and officials have not said who was behind the threats.

items.title: Trump says US military aid to Israel will end this year
items.why: President Trump said on Tuesday that about $4 billion a year in US military funding for Israel will stop at the end of 2026, saying he and Prime Minister Netanyahu agreed it months ago. Netanyahu's office declined to comment. The current aid agreement runs until 2028.
items.matters: Israeli opposition figure Yair Golan says ending the aid would seriously harm Israel's security.

items.title: Indonesian president's chief of staff arrested over alleged phone tapping
items.why: Indonesian police have detained Listyo Sigit Prabowo, President Prabowo Subianto's chief of staff and a former national police chief, and two police generals on suspicion of illegally tapping the phones of the president, ministers and others. The president dismissed him on Wednesday.
items.matters: A presidential spokesman says it may amount to treason; officials say the motive is not yet known.

items.title: European teams say they will not play Russia at ice hockey worlds
items.why: Finland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Latvia and the Czech Republic say they will not play Russia at the 2027 men's world championship, after a sports court ruled on 30 October that Russia must be readmitted. Germany, the host, says it is considering withdrawing.
items.matters: Russia has been banned since invading Ukraine in 2022; the IIHF disagrees with the ruling but says it will comply.
items.changed: Updated: host Germany says it is considering pulling out.

items.title: Philippe Jaenada wins France's Prix Goncourt for a true-crime novel
items.why: The Académie Goncourt gave France's top literary prize to Philippe Jaenada, 62, on 3 November in Paris, by six votes to three. His novel 'L'Inconnue du quai de Javel' investigates the unsolved killing of a young woman found by the Seine in 1949.
items.matters: The prize itself is just €10, but a Goncourt usually turns the winning book into one of France's biggest sellers before Christmas.

items.title: EU court adviser says AI chatbots may infringe news publishers' rights
items.why: An adviser to the EU's top court, Advocate General Maciej Szpunar, said chatbots such as Google's Gemini may breach press publishers' rights when they reuse articles' wording or get past paywalls. He said training AI on such material is generally allowed. The case was brought by Hungarian publisher Like Company.
items.matters: The opinion is not binding, but the court usually follows it; a ruling is expected within months.

sources.name: Court of Justice of the EU

items.title: Saudi Aramco's quarterly profit rises by a third despite attacks
items.why: Saudi Aramco, the state oil company, said net profit for July to September rose about 34% to $36.25 billion, helped by higher oil prices and a one-off gain from a sale to Petronas. Its output fell as attacks hit pipelines and other facilities, Reuters and Euronews report.
items.matters: Saudi Arabia pumped about 8 million barrels of oil a day in September, against just over 10 million before the war.

items.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies after on-field collision
items.why: Jesús de Miguel, a 30-year-old forward for Spanish second-division club Tenerife, died in hospital on 3 November. He was hurt in a collision with Andorra's goalkeeper in stoppage time of a match on the Canary island of Tenerife the evening before. The match was abandoned.
items.matters: Spanish police have opened a routine inquiry; the local chief prosecutor told the agency EFE that criminal charges were unlikely.

items.title: Point of Law, bred by King Charles, wins the Melbourne Cup
items.why: Favourite Point of Law won Australia's richest horse race at Flemington in Melbourne on 3 November by three and three-quarter lengths. Trainer Ciaron Maher also had the second and third horses, Zahrann and Juja Kibo, and jockey Ethan Brown won on his first Cup ride.
items.matters: Maher is the first trainer in 166 runnings to fill the first three places; the King sold the colt this year.

items.title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia pushed back by almost a year
items.why: The Asian Football Confederation said on 3 November that the 2027 men's Asian Cup will now run from 23 December 2027 to 21 January 2028, instead of January 2027. It cited "exceptional circumstances" in the region and travel problems. Saudi Arabia stays as host; FIFA must approve the dates.
items.matters: Reports link the delay to attacks on Saudi Arabia claimed by Yemen's Houthis; other events there have also been moved or postponed.

items.title: Australia's central bank raises interest rates to 4.85%, an 18-year high
items.why: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 0.25 points to 4.85% on Tuesday, its fifth rise this year, in a 6–3 vote. It says inflation, 4.3% in September, will stay above 3% for the coming year.
items.matters: Australia's big four banks raise variable home loan rates from 13 November; ANZ estimates A$79 more a month on a A$500,000 loan.

items.title: Russian strike on Kharkiv hospital injures at least 73, Ukraine says
items.why: A Russian strike hit a city hospital in Kharkiv, in north-eastern Ukraine, at about 03:20 on Tuesday, injuring at least 73 patients, staff and residents, Ukraine's prosecutor general says. President Zelenskyy says Russia launched 289 drones and 76 missiles overnight, mainly at energy sites.
items.matters: Russia's defence ministry says it targeted power facilities supplying Ukraine's army; outages followed in several regions as winter approaches.

items.title: Collins Dictionary names 'mogging' its word of the year
items.why: Collins chose 'mogging', slang for outshining someone or something, as its 2026 word of the year on 3 November. It says use of the word rose 210% this year. Other words on its list include 'carspreading', 'ghost jobs', 'fricy' and 'P(doom)'.
items.matters: The word began in online men's forums but is now mostly used jokingly by younger people, Collins says.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu hits India's Andhra Pradesh coast, at least two dead
items.why: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu came ashore near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh, south-east India, early on 3 November with winds gusting to 120km/h, India's weather department said. State disaster officials told PTI at least two people had died and more than 12,000 were in relief shelters.
items.matters: It is the second cyclone to strike India's east coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab.

items.title: Washington state resident dies of bird flu caught from dairy cattle
items.why: A resident of Yakima County in the US state of Washington has died after catching H5N1 bird flu from infected dairy cows, local health officials say. It is the first US bird flu death this year; two more human cases were confirmed in the county.
items.matters: The US CDC says there is no sign of person-to-person spread and the risk to the public remains low.

items.title: Ukraine says Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia aid point killed at least 37
items.why: Guided bombs hit a school used as an aid point in the village of Komyshuvakha, in south-eastern Ukraine, on Monday as residents gathered for aid, Ukrainian officials say. They now put the dead at 37, with 59 missing. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted Ukrainian military units.
items.matters: The US says Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet for new talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.
items.changed: Updated: officials raised the death toll to 37, with 59 people missing.

items.title: Apple warns rising memory chip costs will squeeze its profit margins
items.why: Apple's revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion in July to September, with iPhone sales up about 17%, in the first results under chief executive John Ternus. But it forecast gross margins of 45–46% for the holiday quarter, as AI demand pushes up memory chip prices.
items.matters: Apple has already raised some iPhone and MacBook prices to offset memory costs, which it expects to keep rising next year.

items.title: Traces of blood molecules found in 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones from Brazil
items.why: A team led by Australia's Curtin University reports heme, part of haemoglobin, inside what it interprets as fossilised red blood cells in the leg bones of Aratasaurus, a feathered dinosaur found in north-east Brazil. The study was published in the journal PNAS.
items.matters: If it holds up, scientists could study the blood and metabolism of extinct animals; some outside experts urge caution.

items.title: NASA's Swift space telescope expected to fall back to Earth today
items.why: NASA's Swift observatory, launched in 2004 to study gamma-ray bursts, was predicted to re-enter the atmosphere around 08:30 GMT on 4 November, give or take 11 hours, the US Space Force says. A commercial mission to boost its sinking orbit failed this summer.
items.matters: Most of it should burn up; NASA puts the chance of anyone being harmed at about 1 in 2,100.

items.title: Karl Bushby reaches home in England after 28-year walk around the world
items.why: British adventurer Karl Bushby arrived at his mother's house in Hull on 2 November, having set off on foot from Punta Arenas in southern Chile in November 1998. AP and Reuters put the journey at about 50,000 km; he swam the English Channel last month to keep it unbroken.
items.matters: He set himself a rule of using no transport at all, crossing four continents and about 30 countries on foot.

items.title: Anthropic reports $17 billion quarterly revenue in updated listing filing
items.why: Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI models, filed an updated US stock market listing document on Monday showing third-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, roughly 12 times a year earlier. It made an operating loss of $567 million and has about $895 billion in commitments, mostly for computing power.
items.matters: Its planned Nasdaq listing, possibly later in November, is widely watched as a test of investor confidence in AI.

items.changed: Updated: Germany, Romania and the UK reported attacks, bringing the total to at least 11 countries.
items.title: Cyberattacks on supermarket fridges spread to at least 11 European countries
items.why: Hackers remotely switched off or heated fridges and freezers at supermarkets in Belgium, Ireland, Italy, Sweden, Germany, Romania and other European countries this week, Al Jazeera and Euronews report. No group has claimed responsibility; the European Commission says the attacks are 'not isolated incidents'.
items.matters: It follows a similar attack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets in October that forced stores to throw away food.

items.changed: Updated: Monday's fall was more than 7%, and prices rose on Tuesday after a reported US strike and Iranian comments.
items.title: Oil prices swing as Iran says a war deal is far off
items.why: Brent crude fell more than 7% on Monday on hopes for Qatar-mediated talks, then rose to about $106 a barrel on Tuesday after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official saying a deal was far off. It was below $104 on Wednesday.
items.matters: Oil prices feed into fuel, flight and food costs worldwide, and Brent ended October at a six-month high.

items.changed: Updated: the election result was certified and Herzog's consultations began.
items.title: Israel certifies election result as Herzog begins coalition talks
items.why: Israel's election committee certified the 27 October results on Wednesday, saying it found no evidence of fraud, after Netanyahu and his allies alleged, without evidence, that the vote was stolen. President Isaac Herzog is holding two days of consultations before choosing who will try to form a government.
items.matters: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's 48; Arab-led parties hold a record 19.

items.changed: Updated: the new wage board meets on Wednesday as protests enter a fourth day.
items.title: Bangladesh wage board meets as garment protests close hundreds of factories
items.why: Bangladesh's new minimum wage board for garment workers was due to hold its first meeting in Dhaka on Wednesday, after four days of protests that have shut several hundred factories. Workers want a monthly minimum of 30,000 taka ($242), up from 12,500. Police have used tear gas, Al Jazeera reports.
items.matters: Garments are Bangladesh's biggest export, and the unrest comes in the peak season for clothing orders.

items.title: Bolivia declares national emergency as El Niño drought hits farming families
items.why: Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz declared a national emergency on 31 October over drought and other El Niño risks. The defence ministry says at least 114,000 families in six of nine departments have been hit since June, with more than 75,000 cattle lost.
items.matters: Officials warn the coming rainy season could bring floods to other parts of the country while dry areas stay parched.
